met_analysis:
The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Murasu” [Pronunciation: Murasu]” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north- northwestwards with a speed of 12 kmph during past 06 hours and lies centered at 1730 hours IST of today, the 02nd November, 2026 over the same region near Latitude 14.7°N and Longitude 80.7°E, about 80 km east- northeast of Nellore (Andhra Pradesh), 80 km east-southeast of Kavali (Andhra Pradesh), 110 km southeast of Ongole (Andhra Pradesh), 190 km north-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu) and 170 km south-southwest of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh). It is very likely to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole during midnight (2330 Hrs IST) of today, the 02nd November to early hours (0400 Hrs IST) of tomorrow, the 3rd November, 2026.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 74°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Eastcentral Arabian Sea adjoining Karnataka-south Maharashtra coasts at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Kerala & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Eastcentral Arabian Sea & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
